title: Retrieve information
summary: Find existing information through a suitable interface, then check that it answers the request.

sections.label: Start with the result
sections.text: Describe what information is needed, its source and the permitted scope. Reuse an approved API when it already supplies the required operation.

sections.label: Choose the approach
sections.text: Structured filters may be enough for ordinary application code. Consider a model step only when interpretation or variable decisions provide a useful contribution.

sections.label: Know what a check establishes
sections.text: OWASP distinguishes checking input structure and business meaning from checking whether the caller has permission. A valid value alone does not establish access.

sections.label: What Atlas can add
sections.text: Open Retrieve and validate, then review Add retrieval checks from your active Factory project. This adds written guidance to selected practices. It does not add an API connection.

sections.label: Coverage
sections.text: The technology entries below illustrate relational and graph approaches. This is a growing selection, not an exhaustive list or a ranking.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended workflow use: Requirements and evidence, Architecture and impact, Tests and review. Use to state the required information and permitted scope, choose a proportionate approved interface and verify the returned result. This is an Atlas recommendation reviewed on 2026-10-15, not a mandatory process or an observed execution result.
Check output to obtain: Record required fields, caller scope, source freshness and expected outcomes for valid, empty and denied requests.
Check output to obtain: Document why the existing API or structured filter is sufficient, or what bounded contribution an optional model must demonstrate.
Check output to obtain: Keep input validity, access permission and returned-data correctness as separate observed checks.

confidence: Documented facts have scoped sources. Suitability for a particular project remains unverified.

catalog.applicability: Use when designing how an application finds existing information through a suitable interface and checks that the result answers the request. Reuse an approved API first and add a model step only when interpretation or variable decisions contribute something useful.
catalog.limits: This is design guidance. It does not connect to a service or prove that a result is correct.

claims.text: Input validation and authorization establish different properties.
